_why: The community prose-tune of the 26B-A4B, seeded 'ranked below the trusted set until
a Lab A/B earns them a real rank' (seed.py community-tunes block). This IS that A/B:
the same battery as gpu-gemma-26b, judged against the same captures. Its handicap is
honest — a Q4_K_M quant of a non-QAT finetune; if the prose does not beat the flagship
in the side-by-side reads, the row is REMOVED (user ruling 2026-07-24: every catalog
row earns its seat by test). ~17.2 GB download on first run. Think-off only — the
think A/B was settled on the flagship battery (no quality gain, 4-10x TTFT).

notes.message: The prose has a lovely, melancholic texture, particularly in the opening metaphor about the lamp lying 'beautifully.'
The first line 'A lamp that will not lie' feels like a stray title fragment that hasn't been integrated into the prose.
Cael's 'sensory' magic—the pressure under the back teeth—is a strong, physical way to establish her abilities without exposition.
The transition between scenes uses asterisks but lacks clear spatial distinction between the shop, the Hall, and the walk home.
Brick's dialogue ('We eat brass wages') is excellent, but Iven's opening lines feel slightly generic compared to the rest of the cast.
The 'lumen-cell' and 'Concern-made' details establish the world's technology and social hierarchy effectively through small details.
The internal monologue during the walk with Nettle ('Because you and I are the same...') is a bit heavy-handed for a first chapter reveal.
Instead of stating Nettle disappeared 'faster than a person could go,' let her physical movement alone convey the supernatural slip.
The prose is exceptionally atmospheric; phrases like 'the way the salt smell of the harbor outlived the tide' establish a strong, melancholic authorial voice.
Cael's competence and her defensive secrecy are immediately clear through her actions with the lamp.
In the opening line, 'A lamp that will not lie' reads more like a title than a sentence; consider integrating it more fluidly into the first paragraph.
The transition to 'The slate board' introduces a new location and cast abruptly; consider a small sensory bridge to ground the shift from the shop to the Hall.
The line 'which Cael tried not to read anything into and read everything into anyway' slips into a slightly omniscient interpretation of her own internal reaction.
Brick's dialogue is functional, but his 'apple' bit is a bit heavy-handed in establishing his 'comfortable' nature.
The concept of 'Facets' and 'Concern seals' provides excellent implicit world-building without over-explaining.
The connection between Nettle's 'gaps' and Cael's 'listening' is powerful; ensure the supernatural stakes don't feel too coincidental in future chapters.
